title: Learning to read in the Shreveport pit and reading for Hayes and Leonard
summary: Lovett says eight years under Mac Daniels in the Shreveport theatre taught him to sight-read, and he had to read for Hayes and Leonard.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: How long had it been before that since you had been reading music with a band?
Well, I guess about seven or eight years in Shreveport, Louisiana.
What was the name of the band there?
It was Mac Daniels' band, Mac Daniels, he was a violin player. And I played in that theater eight years in the pit there.
Because playing in pits you had to read?

If you couldn't read you couldn't play because performers come in there and give you -- just put the music out there, the drum parts and everything and they're gone. They don't stay to rehearse. They're gone after they put it out there and it's up to you to play it that night when they come back so that's the way it was. You have to be, I'd say a sight reader to do that too, you know, because some drummers have had some parts where he wanted to go his way, you understand what I mean, and he'd mark it out there and you'd have to look over all of that kind of stuff and I didn't know whether to play that part or not, see, so I just used my own ideas about it.
